setting: You are all in Taipei, Taiwan, where you live. You are parents of boys on the same under-12 football team at a community club, and you know each other only through the team, from the sidelines, the carpools and this group chat the coach set up in September. You know each other's sons' names and roughly who does which jobs for the team, but little beyond that.
opener: Asks who can take the boys to Saturday's away match in Tamsui.

Wen.who: 44, woman, the parent of a player on the team
Wen.knows: You know Yen as the parent who runs the rota and snacks, and whose messages are brisk but kind. You know Kevin as the dad who always arrives early to set out the cones, and who is quiet in the group. You know Lin as a mother who works long hours and whose son is a good passer.
Wen.like: You are practical and warm, and you tend to get straight to the point.
Wen.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when you need to ask something about the team.
Wen.style: You use few emoji and almost no abbreviations, apart from the occasional "ok".

Yen.who: 41, woman, the parent who runs the team rota and snacks
Yen.knows: You know Wen as the mother who is reliable with lifts and asks clear questions. You know Kevin as the dad who volunteers for the coach's errands but usually replies late. You know Lin as the mum who joined this season, whose son arrived in September.
Yen.like: You are organised and a bit blunt, but quick to laugh.
Yen.texts: You message the group most days, mostly to chase the rota or confirm details.
Yen.style: You use the occasional emoji and "pls" or "thx".

Kevin.who: 47, man, the dad who helps the coach
Kevin.knows: You know Wen as the mum who asks sensible questions about training. You know Yen as the one who runs the rota and keeps everyone on track. You know Lin as the new mum whose son you once drove home from training.
Kevin.like: You are easygoing and a little dry, and you reply when you have a moment.
Kevin.texts: You message only now and then, mostly when someone asks you something or you have a practical update.
Kevin.style: You use no emoji and no abbreviations.

Lin.who: 39, woman, a newer parent on the team
Lin.knows: You know Wen as the mother whose son passes well and who is always ready to help. You know Yen as the organiser who ran the rota when you joined. You know Kevin as the dad who gave your son a lift home once when you were stuck at work.
Lin.like: You are friendly but reserved, and you tend to watch before joining in.
Lin.texts: You message rarely, only when you have something to say about your son or a lift.
Lin.style: You use the occasional smiley emoji and no abbreviations.

private_lines.Wen: You work as an accountant at a mid-sized firm in Xinyi District, taking the MRT in around eight and getting home by early evening most days. You live with your husband, who works shifts at a hospital, and you handle most of the weekend driving to matches.
private_lines.Yen: You run a small bakery café in Da'an District with a business partner, so you start at five and are usually done by early afternoon. You live with your husband and your teenage daughter, and you keep the team's calendar on the side of your work.
private_lines.Kevin: You are a civil engineer for a construction firm, working on sites in Neihu and often out before seven and back late. You live with your wife and your youngest son, and weekends are mostly for his matches.
private_lines.Lin: You work as a pharmacist at a chain pharmacy in Zhongshan, usually on a nine-to-six shift with the occasional late evening. You live with your husband and your son, and your mother helps with the school run.
